title: From Hourly to Annual: How Your Rate Compares to the Average US Salary and Australian Minimum Wage
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay using 38 hours per week. Compare with the average US salary, National Minimum Wage, award rates, and super. Use our timesheet.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour equals $52,254.80 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are higher minimums set for specific industries and occupations, found in pay guides from the Fair Work Ombudsman. Most employees are covered by an award, so their minimum pay is usually above the National Minimum Wage.

faqs.q: Does superannuation count as part of my salary?
faqs.a: No, super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 2026–27, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. It is not included in your take-home pay but is an additional benefit your employer must contribute.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

Whether you are negotiating a salary offer or checking your current pay, converting an hourly rate to an annual figure is straightforward. The basic formula is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks = annual gross pay**

For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This gives you a consistent annual benchmark. For example, an hourly rate of $30.00 becomes $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. If you work part-time, adjust the hours per week accordingly.

While the **average US salary** is often quoted in US dollars, in Australia the Australian Bureau of Statistics reports full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 (May 2026). That equates to roughly $108,352 per year before tax. Comparing your converted annual figure to this average can help you gauge where your pay sits in the broader market.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal floor for employees who are award- or agreement-free. However, most workers are covered by an industry or occupation award, which sets higher minimum rates. For example, the Health Services Award and the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Award have recently updated pay rates.

To find your correct minimum, use the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. These guides list classification-specific rates, allowances, and penalty rates. Your award rate may be significantly above the National Minimum Wage, so always check before relying on the base figure.

### Casual Loading and Super

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the minimum rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that means $33.05 per hour. Our [the timesheet](/) includes a checkbox to add casual loading automatically – never enter a rate that already includes loading.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 2026–27, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is not part of your take-home pay but is an additional benefit you receive as a retirement savings.

## Using the Formula in Practice

To estimate your annual gross pay, use the formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. Then add 12% super on top. For tax, use the 2026–27 resident rates: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% to $135,000; 37% to $190,000; 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator applies these brackets.

Remember: this estimate assumes no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It also does not deduct HELP repayments or the Medicare levy surcharge. Always consult a tax professional for your exact situation.

## Comparing Your Pay to Averages

The ABS average weekly earnings for all employees (including part-time) is $1,579.20 per week, or about $82,118 annually. Full-time ordinary time earnings are higher at $2,083.70 per week ($108,352 per year). These figures are useful context when you convert your own hourly rate. If your annualised pay is below the National Minimum Wage equivalent ($52,255), you may be underpaid. Conversely, if it is above the full-time average, you are earning well above the typical Australian worker.

For more detailed comparisons, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page and [reference tables](/data) with historical data.

## Final Tips

- Always confirm your award coverage using the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog).
- Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to quickly see annual equivalents.
- Remember that super is extra – your employer must pay it on top of your gross salary.
- The [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page explains how to evaluate a total compensation package including super and bonuses.

By understanding the conversion and the benchmarks, you can confidently assess any hourly rate or salary offer.
